Autosomal Agammaglobulinemia

Mendelian MONDO:0011096 Pathograph 83 Show in embeddings browser Primary Immunodeficiency Antibody Deficiency Disorder Congenital Agammaglobulinemia

Autosomal agammaglobulinemia comprises recessive and dominant disorders with severely reduced circulating B cells and antibody production. Defects affect pre-B-cell receptor components, intracellular signaling, transcriptional regulation, zinc transport, or metabolic homeostasis. The developmental stage, residual B-cell output, immunoglobulin concentrations, and accompanying cell defects vary by gene and allele; a single universal pro-B-to-pre-B arrest does not describe the whole group. Recurrent sinopulmonary and invasive bacterial infections are central manifestations, but onset can extend into adulthood. Inflammatory disease and syndromic features occur in selected forms. Immunoglobulin replacement and infection management are the mainstay of care; transplantation requires gene-specific assessment.

Inheritance

2
Autosomal recessive inheritance HP:0000007
Biallelic pathogenic variants underlie IGHM, IGLL1, CD79A, CD79B, BLNK, PIK3R1, PIK3CD, SLC39A7, FNIP1 and recessive TCF3 disease. Consanguineous families have contributed substantially to gene discovery, but consanguinity is not required.
Autosomal recessive inheritance
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:31696364 SUPPORT DIRECT BACKGROUND Human Clinical
"Autosomal recessive agammaglobulinemia (ARA) is a primary immunodeficiency characterized by absent peripheral B cells, severe hypogammaglobulinemia, and absent BTK gene mutations."
Defines the autosomal recessive form of agammaglobulinemia as a distinct, BTK-negative entity.
PMID:31696364 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"In ARA, mutations occur in genes encoding the pre-B cell receptor (pre-BCR) or downstream signaling proteins."
Establishes the pre-BCR / downstream-signalling gene set as the recessive genetic basis.
Autosomal dominant inheritance HP:0000006
Dominant TCF3/E47 disease and SPI1 haploinsufficiency can be de novo or familial; SPI1 disease has variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance. TOP2B-related Hoffman syndrome is another dominant B-cell immunodeficiency. The historical LRRC8A association rests on one truncating-translocation case and currently has Limited gene-disease validity.
Autosomal dominant inheritance
Show evidence (3 references)
PMID:24216514 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"These findings document a mutational hot-spot in E47 and represent an autosomal dominant form of agammaglobulinemia."
Documents an autosomal dominant, dominant-negative form of agammaglobulinemia.
PMID:33951726 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"We studied six unrelated agammaglobulinemic patients, each harboring a heterozygous mutation (four de novo, two unphased) of SPI1, the gene encoding PU.1."
Heterozygous, largely de novo SPI1 variants establish a second autosomal dominant form.
url:https://pure.eur.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/198591090/1-s2.0-S0006497125002174-main.pdf SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"6 were clinically well with laboratory evaluations documenting serum antibody and circulating B-cell concentrations within age- adjusted normal ranges."
Six variant-carrying relatives had normal clinical and laboratory assessments at the study time; ascertainment and possible later onset limit penetrance estimates.

Agammaglobulinemia 5, autosomal dominant (LRRC8A) MONDO:0013290
LRRC8A hgnc:19027 HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (hgnc) Relation: this subtype is caused by variation in this gene This subtype is caused by variation in LRRC8A (hgnc:19027). hgnc:19027 is a gene from the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee.

ClinGen currently classifies the LRRC8A-agammaglobulinemia relationship as Limited. Dominant interference is proposed; neither a specific channel defect nor its mediation of the human immune phenotype was demonstrated.

Does the historical LRRC8A truncation define a reproducible dominant agammaglobulinemia mechanism?
KNOWLEDGE GAP gap_autosomal_agamma_lrrc8a
Attached to
pathophysiology#Truncated LRRC8A Protein
The human claim rests on a single balanced-translocation case. ClinGen labels the relationship Limited. Forced mutant expression and global null mouse studies use different allele mechanisms; preserved null-mouse antibody function cannot establish or refute a dominant human effect. Additional unrelated families and allele-specific functional evidence are needed.

PMID:24752297 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Model Organism

What predicts onset, expressivity and long-term risk in SPI1 carriers?
KNOWLEDGE GAP gap_autosomal_agamma_spi1_penetrance
Attached to
pathophysiology#Reduced PU.1 Dosage or Activity
The 2025 cohort has22 agammaglobulinemic patients,5 relatives with milder antibody abnormalities and6 apparently unaffected relatives. Its81.8% estimate concerns any antibody phenotype and is affected by familial ascertainment and possible later onset. No hematologic malignancy was observed over514 patient-years, but the small cohort cannot establish zero risk. The L180F family has marked within-family variation; a simple PU.1 abundance-to-severity relationship is not established.

Which genetic forms benefit from transplantation, and which compartments must be corrected?
KNOWLEDGE GAP gap_autosomal_agamma_transplant
Attached to
treatments#Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation
ZIP7 sibling outcomes contrast with two SPI1 attempts that did not achieve independence from replacement. Persistent tissue-resident macrophages and donor competitive advantage are proposed explanations in SPI1, not demonstrated mechanisms. Gene-specific outcome data and donor genotype matter; immunologic improvement must be distinguished from skin or other organ recovery.

"(P1 and P2, family 1) additionally showed severe blistering dermatosis (Fig. 1b), failure to thrive and thrombocytopenia, prompting hematopoietic stem cell transplantation; this resulted in cure of immunologic abnormalities and amelioration of skin disease."
Two siblings among six ZIP7-deficient patients had severe skin disease, poor growth and thrombocytopenia; transplantation outcomes are specific to them.
url:https://pure.eur.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/198591090/1-s2.0-S0006497125002174-main.pdf SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical

Biallelic IGHM variants disrupt the membrane heavy-chain component required for early B-cell receptor function. Allele-specific residual expression varies.

Impaired Pre-B-Cell Receptor Assembly
Structural-component defects compromise receptor formation. Direct heterologous evidence here concerns the mature BCR containing the CD79B Q80-stop allele, rather than all patient pre-BCR genotypes.

PMID:10583958 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"Although this patient had normal numbers of pro-B cells, he had no pre-B cells or mature B cells, indicating that BLNK plays a critical role in orchestrating the pro-B cell to pre-B cell transition."
The original BLNK patient had a defined early B-lineage developmental block; this is not an estimate of all alleles or a receptor-assembly assay.

Increased B-Cell 4EBP1 Phosphorylation

Medical Actions

7
Immunoglobulin Replacement Therapy
Action: Immunoglobulin TherapyNCI Thesaurus (NCIT) Relation: this treatment is this clinical intervention This treatment is Immunoglobulin Therapy (NCIT:C62710). NCIT:C62710 is a clinical intervention from the NCI Thesaurus. NCIT:C62710
Platform: Protein replacement
IVIG or SCIG is standard supportive treatment for clinically significant antibody deficiency. Dose and interval are individualized to infections, trough concentrations and lung disease. It supplies passive IgG without restoring the underlying B-cell program; infections and noninfectious complications may persist. The route schedule is extrapolated from XLA guidance, with direct autosomal cohort evidence of continuing replacement dependence.
Mechanism Target:
BYPASSES Reduced Immunoglobulin Production — Passive antibody supplies an effector product without correcting endogenous production or B-cell development.

Consider HSCT only through individualized specialist assessment of the genetic disorder, morbidity, donor genotype and transplant risk. Two severely affected ZIP7 siblings had correction of immunologic abnormalities and improvement of skin disease. Biochemical Markers

5
Serum IgG (Decreased)
Context: Interpret serum IgG against age-specific laboratory intervals, maternal IgG in infancy, infection status and immunoglobulin replacement. Residual or previously normal IgG occurs in later-onset and hypomorphic disease; no single unsupported threshold is imposed here.

"Autosomal recessive agammaglobulinemia (ARA) is a primary immunodeficiency characterized by absent peripheral B cells, severe hypogammaglobulinemia, and absent BTK gene mutations."

Context: Often very low or undetectable, but residual and age-dependent values occur. Serum concentration does not directly measure mucosal secretory IgA.

Peripheral blood CD19+ B cell percentage (Decreased)
Context: Quantify absolute B-cell counts and percentage together with age-aware T/NK subsets. Profound depletion supports the phenotype but is not unique to autosomal agammaglobulinemia; counts may decline over time. Marrow precursor percentages cannot be substituted for peripheral-blood thresholds.

Diagnosis

5
Quantitative serum immunoglobulins
Measure IgG, IgA and IgM with age-specific laboratory interpretation. Maternal IgG, replacement therapy and residual or evolving antibody production affect results.
diagnostic procedure NCIT:C18020 NCI Thesaurus (NCIT)
Markers: Serum IgG, IgA and IgM
Results: Severely reduced endogenous antibody concentrations support the phenotype, with variable residual values.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:31696364 SUPPORT DIRECT BACKGROUND Human Clinical
"Autosomal recessive agammaglobulinemia (ARA) is a primary immunodeficiency characterized by absent peripheral B cells, severe hypogammaglobulinemia, and absent BTK gene mutations."
Severe hypogammaglobulinemia with absent peripheral B cells is the laboratory definition of the disorder.
Lymphocyte subset flow cytometry
Assess absolute and proportional B cells plus T/NK subsets; add lineage-specific studies when indicated. Normal T cells are common but not universal. Repeat testing may reveal progressive B-cell depletion.
flow cytometry NCIT:C16585 NCI Thesaurus (NCIT)
Markers: CD19+ B cell percentage; CD3/CD4/CD8 T cell counts
Results: Profoundly low B cells, with genotype-dependent accompanying abnormalities.

Molecular genetic testing (IEI panel or exome sequencing)
Use phenotype-informed gene testing, multigene panels or exome/genome approaches as appropriate. Evaluate inheritance, copy-number/splice variants and functional evidence; a VUS or a historical gene label alone does not establish causality.

KREC-based newborn screening
KREC testing can detect deficient B-cell output before symptoms in some screening settings. It is a screening adjunct requiring immunophenotypic and molecular confirmation; later-onset forms may not be recognized at birth.

Progression

2
Variable onset and evolving B-cell deficiency
Age: Infancy through adulthood
Many structural pre-BCR defects present early. SPI1 and some TCF3 cases can retain B cells or antibody responses for years before progressing. Diagnostic delay and genuinely later biological onset are distinct.
Show evidence (1 reference)
url:https://pure.eur.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/198591090/1-s2.0-S0006497125002174-main.pdf SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"The 7 remaining late diagnoses developed infectious symptoms later in life, sometimes well into adulthood (range, aged 4-33 years)."
Seven late-diagnosed SPI1 patients developed infectious symptoms later in life; this is a selected gene-specific cohort.
Long-term treated disease
Immunoglobulin replacement often improves infection control, while bronchiectasis, inflammatory complications and gene-specific syndromic findings can persist. The long-term course cannot be summarized as uniformly more severe than XLA.
Show evidence (1 reference)
url:https://pure.eur.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/198591090/1-s2.0-S0006497125002174-main.pdf SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"All patients with PU.MA were IRT dependent"
All 22 agammaglobulinemic patients in this expanded SPI1 cohort required replacement; this is not a trial estimate of all autosomal forms.

Prevalence

1
Worldwide
Unknown
No reliable population rate for this heterogeneous umbrella is established by the cited sources. Historical reviews estimate that XLA accounts for approximately 85% of congenital agammaglobulinemia; the remaining proportion is not a directly measured autosomal population prevalence. Gene discovery, referral patterns, ancestry and later-onset cases affect case composition.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:34241796 SUPPORT DIRECT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Human Clinical
"While the most common cause of congenital agammaglobulinemia is X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA), accounting for approximately 85% of cases, other genetic forms of agammaglobulinemia have been identified."
A review gives an approximate diagnostic share, not an autosomal population prevalence.
⚖️

Clinical Burden

High
Severe infection risk, repeated immunoglobulin infusions and ongoing monitoring impose substantial burden. Chronic lung disease and selected inflammatory or syndromic complications add morbidity. Age at onset, severity and transplant suitability differ by genotype; the umbrella is not uniformly more severe than XLA.
🔀

Differential Diagnoses

8

Conditions with similar clinical presentations that must be differentiated from Autosomal Agammaglobulinemia:

X-linked agammaglobulinemia (BTK) MONDO:0010421
Overlapping Features BTK-related XLA shares severe B-cell and antibody deficiency and is usually male, but rare heterozygous females are affected. Sex, consanguinity and age alone do not distinguish it from all autosomal forms; molecular testing determines the cause.
Show evidence (1 reference)
url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1453/ SUPPORT INDIRECT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Human Clinical
"Females with a heterozygous pathogenic variant in <i>BTK</i> extremely rarely have clinical and laboratory findings of XLA."
The chapter explicitly recognizes rare affected females, correcting an absolute male-only boundary.
Common variable immunodeficiency MONDO:0015517
Overlapping Features CVID generally retains B cells with impaired antibody function, but some autosomal transcription-factor disorders can begin with a CVID-like phenotype and later lose B cells. This is a molecular and longitudinal distinction, not a single universal count threshold.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:39073655 SUPPORT DIRECT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Human Clinical
"TCF3 haploinsufficiency (HI) also impacts both TCF3 isoforms, resulting in common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) with low B cells and hypogammaglobulinemia"
TCF3 allele mechanism can yield an overlapping phenotype.
Severe combined immunodeficiency MONDO:0015974
Overlapping Features Major T-cell deficiency or dysfunction suggests combined immunodeficiency rather than an isolated antibody defect. Some syndromic autosomal forms have additional immune abnormalities, so comprehensive phenotyping and molecular diagnosis remain necessary.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:37273190 SUPPORT DIRECT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Human Clinical
"variants in RAG1 or RAG2 cause severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) because recombination of TCR chains during thymic development is also compromised."
RAG-related T- and B-cell developmental failure distinguishes an important combined-immunodeficiency mechanism.
Transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy Not Yet Curated MONDO:0015698
Overlapping Features Transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy typically retains B cells and is confirmed by subsequent recovery. Severe infections or profound B-cell depletion require evaluation for persistent genetic disease rather than assuming a transient state.
Good syndrome (thymoma with immunodeficiency) MONDO:0015696
Overlapping Features Adult-onset antibody and B-cell deficiency associated with thymoma is an acquired syndromic differential. Adult onset alone does not exclude inherited SPI1 disease.
Secondary hypogammaglobulinemia after B-cell-depleting therapy
Overlapping Features Prior B-cell-depleting therapy can cause prolonged secondary antibody deficiency. Drug exposure, pre-treatment immune history and longitudinal recovery help distinguish it from inherited disease. The cited Greek cohort is broader PAD, not an autosomal agammaglobulinemia prevalence study.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:38792965 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"12 patients with "secondary" hypogammaglobulinemia due to a previous B-cell depletion immunotherapy for autoimmune or malignant disease several years ago"
A national antibody-deficiency cohort documents secondary hypogammaglobulinemia following B-cell depletion therapy as a distinct group requiring separation from primary antibody deficiency.
POU2AF1 (BOB1) deficiency Not Yet Curated MONDO:0800146
Overlapping Features BOB1 deficiency can cause agammaglobulinemia despite preserved peripheral B-cell numbers, reflecting a later functional differentiation defect rather than the B-cell-poor pattern emphasized here.
Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:37273190 SUPPORT DIRECT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Human Clinical
"Despite normal numbers of peripheral B cells, the OBF-1–deficient patient presented with recurrent respiratory infection, agammaglobulinemia, and an absence of class switched memory B cells (Kury et al., 2021)."
A review summarizes the reported BOB1 patient; the original brief report had no substantive retrievable cached text.
Hyper-IgM syndrome Not Yet Curated MONDO:0003947
Overlapping Features Class-switch defects usually preserve B-cell numbers and IgM relative to IgG/IgA. Residual IgM alone does not exclude evolving autosomal agammaglobulinemia; use the full immunophenotype and genotype.

description: Autosomal agammaglobulinemia comprises recessive and dominant disorders with severely reduced circulating B cells and antibody production. Defects affect pre-B-cell receptor components, intracellular signaling, transcriptional regulation, zinc transport, or metabolic homeostasis. The developmental stage, residual B-cell output, immunoglobulin concentrations, and accompanying cell defects vary by gene and allele; a single universal pro-B-to-pre-B arrest does not describe the whole group. Recurrent sinopulmonary and invasive bacterial infections are central manifestations, but onset can extend into adulthood. Inflammatory disease and syndromic features occur in selected forms. Immunoglobulin replacement and infection management are the mainstay of care; transplantation requires gene-specific assessment.

    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
- name: Autosomal dominant inheritance
  description: Dominant TCF3/E47 disease and SPI1 haploinsufficiency can be de novo or familial; SPI1 disease has variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance. TOP2B-related Hoffman syndrome is another dominant B-cell immunodeficiency. The historical LRRC8A association rests on one truncating-translocation case and currently has Limited gene-disease validity.

prevalence:
- population: Worldwide
  measure_type: UNKNOWN
  notes: No reliable population rate for this heterogeneous umbrella is established by the cited sources. Historical reviews estimate that XLA accounts for approximately 85% of congenital agammaglobulinemia; the remaining proportion is not a directly measured autosomal population prevalence. Gene discovery, referral patterns, ancestry and later-onset cases affect case composition.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34241796
    reference_title: 'Agammaglobulinemia: from X-linked to Autosomal Forms of Disease.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: While the most common cause of congenital agammaglobulinemia is X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA), accounting for approximately 85% of cases, other genetic forms of agammaglobulinemia have been identified.
    explanation: A review gives an approximate diagnostic share, not an autosomal population prevalence.

- name: Ig-Beta Deficiency

  evidence:

- name: Defective TCF3 Transcription-Factor Activity
  description: Dominant E47 E555K impairs tested E-box binding/transactivation and interferes with wild-type E47. Recessive loss affects both E12 and E47; heterozygous haploinsufficiency can instead produce CVID-like disease. These allele mechanisms are not interchangeable.
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24216514
    reference_title: A recurrent dominant negative E47 mutation causes agammaglobulinemia and BCR(-) B cells.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: These findings document a mutational hot-spot in E47 and represent an autosomal dominant form of agammaglobulinemia.
    explanation: Establishes the dominant TCF3/E47 form.
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:24216514
    reference_title: A recurrent dominant negative E47 mutation causes agammaglobulinemia and BCR(-) B cells.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: Although E555K E47 did not bind to the μE5 or creatinine kinase probes as a homodimer, it did allow MyoD to bind to the creatinine kinase probe (Figure 3D).
    explanation: E555K disrupts measured homodimer DNA binding while preserving the tested MyoD heterodimer interaction; it is not loss of all E-protein partnerships.
  - reference: PMID:39073655
    reference_title: Exclusive Characteristics of the p.E555K Dominant-Negative Variant in Autosomal Dominant E47 Deficiency.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS

- name: Reduced PU.1 Dosage or Activity
  description: SPI1 haploinsufficiency can arise through protein instability, localization defects or impaired DNA binding, depending on the allele. Reporter coexpression did not demonstrate dominant interference. The human phenotype ranges from unaffected carriers to progressive B-cell aplasia.
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33951726
    reference_title: Constrained chromatin accessibility in PU.1-mutated agammaglobulinemia patients.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: We studied six unrelated agammaglobulinemic patients, each harboring a heterozygous mutation (four de novo, two unphased) of SPI1, the gene encoding PU.1.
    explanation: The original SPI1 cohort establishes the human genetic association; later families show inherited variants and milder phenotypes.
  - reference: PMID:33951726
    reference_title: Constrained chromatin accessibility in PU.1-mutated agammaglobulinemia patients.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Patient SPI1 mutations encoded destabilized PU.1 proteins unable to nuclear localize or bind target DNA.
    explanation: Functional assays identify allele-dependent protein instability, localization or DNA-binding defects; no single defect applies to every variant.
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: url:https://pure.eur.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/198591090/1-s2.0-S0006497125002174-main.pdf

    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    directness: DIRECT

    explanation: Six variant-carrying relatives had normal clinical and laboratory assessments at the study time; ascertainment and possible later onset limit penetrance estimates.

      label: SPI1

- name: Restricted B-Lineage Chromatin Accessibility
  description: ATAC-seq in edited RS4;11 pro-B leukemia cells links reduced PU.1 dose to a less accessible B-lineage regulatory landscape. Cell-line gene-network effects support a developmental model but are not direct chromatin measurements in all patients.
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33951726
    reference_title: Constrained chromatin accessibility in PU.1-mutated agammaglobulinemia patients.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: PU.1 OCRs were significantly more accessible in SPI1+/+ than SPI1+/− or SPI1−/− cell lines
    explanation: ATAC-seq in edited RS4;11 pro-B leukemia cells shows a PU.1-dose-associated accessibility difference.
  - reference: PMID:33951726
    reference_title: Constrained chromatin accessibility in PU.1-mutated agammaglobulinemia patients.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: we employed assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq) to generate genome-wide chromatin accessibility maps of human RS4;11 pro–B cell lines either unedited (SPI1+/+) or CRISPR/Cas9 edited with monoallelic (SPI1+/−) or biallelic (SPI1−/−) SPI1 exon one indels that abolished PU.1 expression.
    explanation: ATAC-seq compared transformed RS4;11 pro-B cell lines with monoallelic or biallelic engineered disruption; these are not patient-cell chromatin maps.
  downstream:
  - target: Impaired B-Cell Development
    description: Chromatin restriction is proposed to constrain the transcriptional program needed for B-cell progression. Patient phenotype and edited HSPC experiments support the model without proving every intervening regulatory target.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:33951726
      reference_title: Constrained chromatin accessibility in PU.1-mutated agammaglobulinemia patients.

      snippet: PU.1 OCRs were significantly more accessible in SPI1+/+ than SPI1+/− or SPI1−/− cell lines
      explanation: ATAC-seq in edited RS4;11 pro-B leukemia cells shows a PU.1-dose-associated accessibility difference.
    - reference: PMID:33951726
      reference_title: Constrained chromatin accessibility in PU.1-mutated agammaglobulinemia patients.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: Introducing disease-similar SPI1 mutations into human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells impaired early in vitro B cell and myeloid cell differentiation.
      explanation: Edited cord-blood progenitors carry mixtures of near-variant indels, not precise patient-allele knock-ins; lineage selection supports but does not isolate the chromatin mediator.

- name: Truncated LRRC8A Protein
  description: One human balanced translocation generated a truncated LRRC8A protein alongside wild-type protein. The gene-disease relationship remains Limited. Dominant interference is a hypothesis supported by a forced-expression mouse experiment, not an established universal channel mechanism.
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:14660746
    reference_title: A congenital mutation of the novel gene LRRC8 causes agammaglobulinemia in humans.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: These results indicate that LRRC8 is responsible for the B cell deficiency in this patient and is required for B cell development.
    explanation: The original authors interpreted their single human case and mutant-expression model as causal; current ClinGen validity remains Limited.
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: url:https://thegencc.org/submissions/SGC-107391.2
    reference_title: LRRC8A | agammaglobulinemia | Autosomal dominant by ClinGen submission information facts
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: Since other patients with B cell deficiency and heterozygous LRRC8A have not been identified, the curation is classified as Limited.
    explanation: ClinGen explains the Limited classification by the lack of additional human cases.
  genes:

  description: Heterozygous TOPRIM-domain TOP2B variants cause Hoffman syndrome. Yeast growth and decatenation experiments support loss of activity with partial dominant interference. Human B-cell enzyme activity and marrow arrest stage were not directly measured.

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: In three families with Hoffman syndrome 9,10, we identi ﬁed three heterozygous mutations affecting the TOPRIM, or DNA gating, domain of the type II topoisomerase TOP2B.

- name: Impaired B-Cell Development
  description: Different autosomal defects reduce B-lineage progression at different stages. A pro-B-to-pre-B block fits several structural/adaptor disorders, but ZIP7, PIK3R1, FNIP1 and progressive SPI1 disease show distinct patterns. The umbrella does not imply a universal complete arrest.
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:31696364
    reference_title: Genetic Approaches for Definitive Diagnosis of Agammaglobulinemia in Consanguineous Families.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Autosomal recessive agammaglobulinemia (ARA) is a primary immunodeficiency characterized by absent peripheral B cells, severe hypogammaglobulinemia, and absent BTK gene mutations.
    explanation: The cited source describes the B-cell and antibody-deficiency phenotype. No frequency band or universal complete absence is inferred.
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
  - reference: PMID:10583958
    reference_title: An essential role for BLNK in human B cell development.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Although this patient had normal numbers of pro-B cells, he had no pre-B cells or mature B cells, indicating that BLNK plays a critical role in orchestrating the pro-B cell to pre-B cell transition.
    explanation: The original BLNK patient had a defined early B-lineage developmental block; this is not an estimate of all alleles or a receptor-assembly assay.
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT

- name: Biallelic SLC39A7 Variants
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: Biallelic hypomorphic or truncating SLC39A7 variants define this genetic subtype. The reported viable patients should not be described as proven complete ZIP7 knockouts.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30718914
    reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    directness: DIRECT
    snippet: Six individuals from 5 kindreds of white European, South Asian or Hispanic ancestry, were found to harbor compound heterozygous (4 families) or homozygous (1 family) rare variants in SLC39A7
    explanation: Six affected people from five kindreds carry biallelic variants.
  role: trigger
  downstream:
  - target: Reduced ZIP7 Zinc Transport
    description: Tested human alleles impair transporter function.
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:30718914
      reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      directness: DIRECT
      snippet: In keeping with hypomorphic behavior, the Zn2+ signal generated by either mutant ZIP7 was significantly reduced compared with WT (Fig. 2h), despite similar amounts of protein expression
      explanation: The P190A and E363K transport assays show reduced reporter signal at comparable protein expression.
  - target: Abnormal Skin Blistering
    description: Severe ZIP7 disease is associated with this clinical feature; organ-specific intermediates are unresolved.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:30718914
      reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: (P1 and P2, family 1) additionally showed severe blistering dermatosis (Fig. 1b), failure to thrive and thrombocytopenia, prompting hematopoietic stem cell transplantation; this resulted in cure of immunologic abnormalities and amelioration of skin disease.
      explanation: Two siblings among six ZIP7-deficient patients had severe skin disease, poor growth and thrombocytopenia; transplantation outcomes are specific to them.

- name: Reduced ZIP7 Zinc Transport
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: Reduced zinc transport was measured for human P190A and E363K. Residual expression and ER localization distinguish transport impairment from universal protein absence.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30718914
    reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    directness: DIRECT
    snippet: In keeping with hypomorphic behavior, the Zn2+ signal generated by either mutant ZIP7 was significantly reduced compared with WT (Fig. 2h), despite similar amounts of protein expression
    explanation: The P190A and E363K transport assays show reduced reporter signal at comparable protein expression.
  downstream:
  - target: Reduced B-Cell Cytosolic Free Zinc
    description: Reduced transport is associated with deficient cytosolic zinc in the mouse cellular model; compartmental buffering and compensation were not fully resolved.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:30718914
      reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      directness: INDIRECT
      snippet: Cytoplasmic Zn2+ concentrations were indeed lower in mutant compared to WT cells, whereas ER Zn2+ amounts were equivalent
      explanation: FRET-FLIM in IL7-expanded mutant mouse marrow B-cell cultures measures lower free cytosolic zinc with unchanged free ER zinc.
- name: Reduced B-Cell Cytosolic Free Zinc
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: Mutant mouse B-cell cultures have lower free cytosolic zinc. This is not evidence of systemic zinc deficiency, excess free ER zinc or a measured local zinc pulse.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30718914
    reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    directness: DIRECT
    snippet: Cytoplasmic Zn2+ concentrations were indeed lower in mutant compared to WT cells, whereas ER Zn2+ amounts were equivalent
    explanation: FRET-FLIM in IL7-expanded mutant mouse marrow B-cell cultures measures lower free cytosolic zinc with unchanged free ER zinc.
  downstream:
  - target: Increased B-Cell Phosphatase Activity
    description: Loss of zinc-mediated phosphatase inhibition is a proposed partial mediator. No selective zinc restoration experiment proves necessity.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:30718914
      reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      directness: INDIRECT
      snippet: Our data suggest that ZIP7 hypofunction likewise impedes signalling by the nascent BCR during positive selection, and that this may be in part due to defective Zn2+-dependent inhibition of phosphatase activity.
      explanation: The authors propose partial zinc/phosphatase mediation; PTEN haploinsufficiency did not rescue development.
- name: Increased B-Cell Phosphatase Activity
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: Developing mutant B cells show increased constitutive activity on a broad phosphatase substrate. Specific PTEN hyperactivity is not isolated by this assay.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30718914
    reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    directness: DIRECT
    snippet: Constitutive phosphatase activity was indeed higher in ZIP7P198A/P198A compared to WT pre-B and immature B cells, as measured by flow cytometry using a cell-permeable alkaline phosphatase substrate
    explanation: The broad live phosphatase-substrate assay does not isolate PTEN activity.
  downstream:
  - target: Reduced B-Cell Receptor Signaling
    description: Elevated phosphatase activity may contribute to reduced signaling, but multiple pathways remain involved and the PTEN-only rescue experiment was negative.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:30718914
      reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      directness: INDIRECT
      snippet: Our data suggest that ZIP7 hypofunction likewise impedes signalling by the nascent BCR during positive selection, and that this may be in part due to defective Zn2+-dependent inhibition of phosphatase activity.
      explanation: The authors propose partial zinc/phosphatase mediation; PTEN haploinsufficiency did not rescue development.
- name: Reduced B-Cell Receptor Signaling
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: Antigen-stimulated immature mutant B cells have reduced phosphorylation of SYK, PLCγ2 and ERK despite equivalent surface receptor expression. These are parallel signaling readouts rather than demonstrated intrinsic kinase defects.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30718914
    reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    directness: DIRECT
    snippet: immature ZIP7P198A/P198A SWHel B cells showed impaired antigen-induced signalling as judged by reduced amounts of multiple phosphorylated intermediates, including SYK, PLCγ2 and ERK
    explanation: Ex-vivo antigen stimulation demonstrates reduced phosphorylation despite comparable surface BCR.
  downstream:
  - target: Impaired ZIP7-Dependent B-Cell Maturation
    description: Deficient nascent-BCR signaling is proposed to impair positive selection. This is not a fully isolated necessary sequence.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:30718914
      reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
      supports: SUPPORT

      explanation: The authors propose partial zinc/phosphatase mediation; PTEN haploinsufficiency did not rescue development.
- name: Impaired ZIP7-Dependent B-Cell Maturation
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: ZIP7 hypofunction blocks B-cell development, most clearly at late pre-B to immature transition in mixed marrow chimeras; an earlier contribution cannot be excluded.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30718914
    reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    directness: DIRECT
    snippet: Eight weeks after BM transfer, our analysis confirmed a B cell intrinsic block in development, which was most evident in a failure to progress from the late pre-B (FrD) to immature B (FrE) cell stage, with no residual mutant cells in the recirculating FrF population
    explanation: Mixed marrow chimeras show cell-intrinsic developmental failure strongest at late-pre-B to immature transition.
  role: central_effector
  downstream:
  - target: Reduced Circulating B-Cell Output
    description: Mouse late-pre-B/immature maturation failure and human B-cell depletion support reduced output, without imposing one stage on all autosomal forms.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:30718914
      reference_title: An essential role for the Zn(2+) transporter ZIP7 in B cell development.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      directness: INDIRECT
      snippet: Eight weeks after BM transfer, our analysis confirmed a B cell intrinsic block in development, which was most evident in a failure to progress from the late pre-B (FrD) to immature B (FrE) cell stage, with no residual mutant cells in the recirculating FrF population
      explanation: Mixed marrow chimeras show cell-intrinsic developmental failure strongest at late-pre-B to immature transition.
- name: Increased B-Cell Mitochondrial Abundance
  description: Mitochondrial abundance was increased in rare circulating B cells from one FNIP1-deficient patient. This is not a measure in marrow progenitors or cardiac tissue.
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://repositorio.udd.cl/server/api/core/bitstreams/a9d54a3e-518c-4beb-ac3d-b570765e7314/content
    reference_title: https://repositorio.udd.cl/server/api/core/bitstreams/a9d54a3e-518c-4beb-ac3d-b570765e7314/content
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: Indeed, circulating P1 B-cells exhibited increased numbers of mitochondria and mitochondrial activity relative to healthy control (HC) B-cells (Figure 1F and supplemental Figure 9 ).
    explanation: Mitochondrial dye readouts were measured in rare circulating B cells from one patient compared with a healthy control; they do not establish a general ATP-production flux.
- name: Increased B-Cell Mitochondrial Activity Signal
  description: A mitochondrial activity-associated dye readout was increased in circulating B cells from one FNIP1-deficient patient. It is distinct from mitochondrial abundance and does not establish increased ATP synthesis or respiratory flux.
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://repositorio.udd.cl/server/api/core/bitstreams/a9d54a3e-518c-4beb-ac3d-b570765e7314/content

    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: Indeed, circulating P1 B-cells exhibited increased numbers of mitochondria and mitochondrial activity relative to healthy control (HC) B-cells (Figure 1F and supplemental Figure 9 ).
    explanation: Mitochondrial dye readouts were measured in rare circulating B cells from one patient compared with a healthy control; they do not establish a general ATP-production flux.
- name: Increased B-Cell AKT Phosphorylation
  description: Marrow B-cell progenitors from one FNIP1-deficient patient had increased AKT Ser473 phosphorylation relative to a healthy control. This is an observed signaling state, not a direct assay of a unique kinase mechanism.
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://repositorio.udd.cl/server/api/core/bitstreams/a9d54a3e-518c-4beb-ac3d-b570765e7314/content
    reference_title: https://repositorio.udd.cl/server/api/core/bitstreams/a9d54a3e-518c-4beb-ac3d-b570765e7314/content
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: Specifically, p4EBP1 and pAkt473 were significantly activated ( 12.46±1.86 vs 4.00±0.53, p = 0.00 02; 3.82±1.78 vs 0.97±0. 09, p = 0.029). As opposite, no difference could be found in S6 phosphorylation (1.46±0.14 vs 2.70±0.51, p = 0.14).
    explanation: One patient marrow comparison showed increased p4EBP1 and pAKT473 but not pS6; small repeated assays do not expand the donor count.
- name: Increased B-Cell 4EBP1 Phosphorylation
  description: Marrow B-cell progenitors from one FNIP1-deficient patient had increased 4EBP1 phosphorylation; pS6 was not significantly altered. BEZ235 lowered the 4EBP1 readout without demonstrating restored B-cell development or clinical benefit.
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  evidence:

    explanation: One patient marrow comparison showed increased p4EBP1 and pAKT473 but not pS6; small repeated assays do not expand the donor count.
phenotypes:
- name: Agammaglobulinemia
  category: Immunologic
  description: Markedly impaired endogenous antibody production defines the severe phenotype. Some isotypes remain measurable, especially in evolving or hypomorphic disease.
  diagnostic: true
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Agammaglobulinemia
    term:
      id: HP:0004432
      label: Agammaglobulinemia
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:31696364
    reference_title: Genetic Approaches for Definitive Diagnosis of Agammaglobulinemia in Consanguineous Families.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Autosomal recessive agammaglobulinemia (ARA) is a primary immunodeficiency characterized by absent peripheral B cells, severe hypogammaglobulinemia, and absent BTK gene mutations.
    explanation: The cited source describes the B-cell and antibody-deficiency phenotype. No frequency band or universal complete absence is inferred.
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
- name: Decreased Total B Cell Count
  category: Immunologic
  description: Severely reduced circulating B cells, assessed by age-aware absolute counts and proportions. Residual cells and progressive loss occur; this finding alone does not distinguish every genetic or acquired cause.

    directness: DIRECT

- name: Serum IgG
  presence: Decreased
  context: Interpret serum IgG against age-specific laboratory intervals, maternal IgG in infancy, infection status and immunoglobulin replacement. Residual or previously normal IgG occurs in later-onset and hypomorphic disease; no single unsupported threshold is imposed here.
  biomarker_term:
    preferred_term: Immunoglobulin G Measurement
    term:
      id: NCIT:C81971
      label: Immunoglobulin G Measurement
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:31696364
    reference_title: Genetic Approaches for Definitive Diagnosis of Agammaglobulinemia in Consanguineous Families.

differential_diagnoses:
- name: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (BTK)
  description: BTK-related XLA shares severe B-cell and antibody deficiency and is usually male, but rare heterozygous females are affected. Sex, consanguinity and age alone do not distinguish it from all autosomal forms; molecular testing determines the cause.
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: Bruton-type agammaglobulinemia
    term:
      id: MONDO:0010421
      label: Bruton-type agammaglobulinemia
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1453/
    reference_title: X-Linked Agammaglobulinemia - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: Females with a heterozygous pathogenic variant in <i>BTK</i> extremely rarely have clinical and laboratory findings of XLA.
    explanation: The chapter explicitly recognizes rare affected females, correcting an absolute male-only boundary.
- name: Common variable immunodeficiency
  description: CVID generally retains B cells with impaired antibody function, but some autosomal transcription-factor disorders can begin with a CVID-like phenotype and later lose B cells. This is a molecular and longitudinal distinction, not a single universal count threshold.
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: common variable immunodeficiency
    term:
      id: MONDO:0015517
      label: common variable immunodeficiency
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39073655
    reference_title: Exclusive Characteristics of the p.E555K Dominant-Negative Variant in Autosomal Dominant E47 Deficiency.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: TCF3 haploinsufficiency (HI) also impacts both TCF3 isoforms, resulting in common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) with low B cells and hypogammaglobulinemia
    explanation: TCF3 allele mechanism can yield an overlapping phenotype.
- name: Severe combined immunodeficiency
  description: Major T-cell deficiency or dysfunction suggests combined immunodeficiency rather than an isolated antibody defect. Some syndromic autosomal forms have additional immune abnormalities, so comprehensive phenotyping and molecular diagnosis remain necessary.
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: severe combined immunodeficiency
    term:
      id: MONDO:0015974
      label: severe combined immunodeficiency
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37273190
    reference_title: Inborn errors of human B cell development, differentiation, and function.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: variants in RAG1 or RAG2 cause severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) because recombination of TCR chains during thymic development is also compromised.
    explanation: RAG-related T- and B-cell developmental failure distinguishes an important combined-immunodeficiency mechanism.
- name: Transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy
  description: Transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy typically retains B cells and is confirmed by subsequent recovery. Severe infections or profound B-cell depletion require evaluation for persistent genetic disease rather than assuming a transient state.
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy
    term:
      id: MONDO:0015698
      label: transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy
- name: Good syndrome (thymoma with immunodeficiency)
  description: Adult-onset antibody and B-cell deficiency associated with thymoma is an acquired syndromic differential. Adult onset alone does not exclude inherited SPI1 disease.
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: Good syndrome
    term:
      id: MONDO:0015696
      label: Good syndrome
- name: Secondary hypogammaglobulinemia after B-cell-depleting therapy
  description: Prior B-cell-depleting therapy can cause prolonged secondary antibody deficiency. Drug exposure, pre-treatment immune history and longitudinal recovery help distinguish it from inherited disease. The cited Greek cohort is broader PAD, not an autosomal agammaglobulinemia prevalence study.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38792965
    reference_title: A Nationwide Study of the Delayed Diagnosis and the Clinical Manifestations of Predominantly Antibody Deficiencies and CTLA4-Mediated Immune Dysregulation Syndrome in Greece.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 12 patients with "secondary" hypogammaglobulinemia due to a previous B-cell depletion immunotherapy for autoimmune or malignant disease several years ago
    explanation: A national antibody-deficiency cohort documents secondary hypogammaglobulinemia following B-cell depletion therapy as a distinct group requiring separation from primary antibody deficiency.
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
- name: POU2AF1 (BOB1) deficiency
  description: BOB1 deficiency can cause agammaglobulinemia despite preserved peripheral B-cell numbers, reflecting a later functional differentiation defect rather than the B-cell-poor pattern emphasized here.
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: agammaglobulinemia, autosomal recessive, due to BOB1 deficiency
    term:
      id: MONDO:0800146
      label: agammaglobulinemia, autosomal recessive, due to BOB1 deficiency
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37273190
    reference_title: Inborn errors of human B cell development, differentiation, and function.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: Despite normal numbers of peripheral B cells, the OBF-1–deficient patient presented with recurrent respiratory infection, agammaglobulinemia, and an absence of class switched memory B cells (Kury et al., 2021).
    explanation: A review summarizes the reported BOB1 patient; the original brief report had no substantive retrievable cached text.
- name: Hyper-IgM syndrome
  description: Class-switch defects usually preserve B-cell numbers and IgM relative to IgG/IgA. Residual IgM alone does not exclude evolving autosomal agammaglobulinemia; use the full immunophenotype and genotype.
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: hyper-IgM syndrome
    term:
      id: MONDO:0003947
      label: hyper-IgM syndrome
treatments:
- name: Immunoglobulin Replacement Therapy
  description: IVIG or SCIG is standard supportive treatment for clinically significant antibody deficiency. Dose and interval are individualized to infections, trough concentrations and lung disease. It supplies passive IgG without restoring the underlying B-cell program; infections and noninfectious complications may persist. The route schedule is extrapolated from XLA guidance, with direct autosomal cohort evidence of continuing replacement dependence.
  therapeutic_modality: PROTEIN_REPLACEMENT
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Immunoglobulin Therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C62710
      label: Immunoglobulin Therapy
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Reduced Immunoglobulin Production
    treatment_effect: BYPASSES
    description: Passive antibody supplies an effector product without correcting endogenous production or B-cell development.
    evidence:
    - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1453/
      reference_title: X-Linked Agammaglobulinemia - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      snippet: The mainstay of treatment is gammaglobulin substitution therapy (by weekly subcutaneous injection or intravenous infusion every two to four weeks) to prevent bacterial infections.
      explanation: GeneReviews expert guidance is for XLA; shared antibody-replacement principles are extrapolated to autosomal disease.
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK1453/
    reference_title: X-Linked Agammaglobulinemia - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
